title: Robust Agentic AI: An Architectural Framework Using MCP and Deterministic Safety Guardrails in the Context of Mining in Industry 4.0
V81_REASON: MCAF explicitly places deterministic LogicGuard runtime enforcement based on Linear Temporal Logic between agentic reasoning and safety-critical mining execution. This is directly aligned with execution-boundary validity/safety gating, but the paper is presented as an architectural/position framework rather than validated primary deployment evidence; retain for core-mechanism review without promoting to empirical CORE.
V81_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: SciTePress ICEIS 2026 publisher abstract and full-text record

title: Integrated Framework for Secure Communication among Multiple Agents using MCP and A2A
V81_REASON: Source-backed bibliographic evidence confirms an integrated MCP/A2A secure multi-agent communication framework, but publicly recovered evidence is insufficient to establish whether security controls enforce authorization or revalidation at consequential tool/action execution rather than secure communication generally.
V81_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: ICICI 2026 DOI-confirmed bibliographic/author record; full method evidence unavailable

title: An Agent Framework for Fault Recovery Planning Generation Based on Model Context Protocol
V81_REASON: The paper is source-confirmed as an MCP-based agent framework for fault-recovery planning, but accessible evidence does not establish whether generated plans are autonomously executed, whether current state is revalidated before execution, or whether post-action effects are verified. No stronger classification is forced.
V81_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: DBLP/IEEE ISCAS 2026 bibliographic record; method/full-text evidence insufficient

title: Agentic AI for Scalable and Robust Optical Systems Control
V81_REASON: AgentOptics executes protocol-compliant actions on heterogeneous optical devices and demonstrates monitoring, closed-loop optimization, robustness and error handling. Recovered evidence establishes real control and recovery-oriented performance but not an explicit authority/premise/admissibility revalidation gate for a pending consequential action.

title: Enhancing Cybersecurity Incident Response Efficiency Through Autonomous Agentic AI: Design, Implementation, and Evaluation with Wazuh SIEM
V81_REASON: Phase 2 extends the MCP/Wazuh workflow to autonomous active responses including IP blocking and account disabling, so the system clearly crosses into consequential external effects. However, recovered evidence does not establish a distinct runtime validity/authority revalidation mechanism governing those actions before commit.

title: Adaptive Takeover Time Budget Allocation in Automated Driving: A Physiology-Aware Semantic Agent Framework
V81_REASON: P-SA continuously combines physiological readiness and driving context to adapt takeover-time budgets for SAE Level-3 handover. This is high-stakes state-aware decision support, but recovered evidence does not establish that the agent itself commits vehicle-control transfer through an explicit execution-boundary validity/authority gate.

title: MCP-Edge: Extending the Model Context Protocol to Constrained IoT Devices
V81_REASON: MCP-Edge enables agents to discover and invoke physical IoT-device capabilities through MCP/MCP-Lite, including state-changing device tools. Its contribution is protocol/transport interoperability for constrained hardware; recovered evidence does not show decision-validity revalidation before physical effects.
V81_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: IEEE Cloud Summit abstract/summary; MCP-Edge reference implementation documentation

title: A Think-Do Architecture for Cognitive Autonomy: LLM-Driven Agentic AI for Sustainable Resource Orchestration in 6G Satellite Networks
V81_REASON: The proposed Think-Do architecture separates LLM semantic reasoning from real-time execution algorithms for adaptive satellite-resource orchestration and discusses MCP-enabled collaboration. It is an architectural vision and does not provide evidence of an execution-time validity/authority revalidation mechanism for pending consequential actions.

title: SQL-MCP: An AI-Powered Multi-LLM Framework for Autonomous Oracle Database Object Debugging Using GPT-4 and Claude
V81_REASON: Specialist-Validator-Arbiter cross-model validation, hallucination detection, consensus arbitration and human-in-the-loop governance are strongly relevant, and the system reports autonomous fix success. Accessible evidence does not establish whether validated fixes are actually committed to live database objects or remain generated/debugging outputs, so the consequential decision-to-effect boundary cannot yet be adjudicated safely.
V81_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: AIIoT 2026 DOI-confirmed abstract/summary; full execution semantics unavailable

title: Architectural Invariants for Designing Multi-Agent Energy Management Systems in Microgrids
V81_REASON: The architecture explicitly separates A2A decision coordination from MCP data/service access and physical control, with a supervisor agent ensuring decision consistency. The study is qualitative and identifies quantitative validation and experimental deployment as future work; it therefore lacks demonstrated decision-validity enforcement across a real execution boundary.
V81_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: IRASET 2026 DOI-confirmed abstract and accessible paper text
